Who it's for

What you'll learn

One day. Practical, applicable, field-ready.

Each module combines classroom explanation with hands-on demonstration. Sessions are tailored to the group — a waterwell team covers different ground conditions than an HDD crew.

Module 01
Drilling Fluid Fundamentals
  • What drilling fluids actually do (and why it matters)
  • Bentonite vs polymer — when and why
  • Reading fluid properties: viscosity, density, pH, gel strength
  • Marsh funnel testing — how to do it right on site
Module 02
Ground Conditions & Fluid Selection
  • Matching fluid to ground — sand, clay, rock, volcanic, reactive formations
  • Why the same fluid behaves differently in different soils
  • Designing a fluid program before the first rod turns
  • When to change strategy mid-bore
Module 03
Mixing, Dosage & Additives
  • How to mix correctly — sequence, hydration, timing
  • Dosage ranges and when to go high or low
  • When to add clay inhibitors, soda ash, defoamers
  • Common mixing mistakes and how to spot them
Module 04
On-Site Troubleshooting
  • Hole collapse — causes and real fixes
  • Loss of circulation — how to respond, not just react
  • Stuck pipe — prevention and fluid factors
  • Viscosity problems — too thick, too thin, why it changes
Module 05
Environmental & Compliance
  • Fluid disposal — what's legal, what's not, and what MetaFLO solves
  • NSF/ANSI certification — when it matters and why
  • Spill response and site management
  • Documenting what you mixed and when
Module 06
Program Design Workshop
  • Live design exercise — real bore specs, group problem-solving
  • How to write a fluid program for a tender
  • Reviewing and adjusting mid-project
  • When to call Blick and what information to have ready

Common questions

What to know before you register.

If you don't see your question here, call us — we're happy to talk through whether Mud School is right for you or your team.

Is there a cost to attend?

Mud School is run by Blick as a service to the industry. There is no charge to attend — we believe knowledge shared makes everyone better. Some sessions may require a small venue contribution for hosted formats. We'll confirm details when sessions are confirmed.

How long is a session?

Sessions are typically a full day — starting around 8am and wrapping by 4–4:30pm. This gives enough time to cover theory, do hands-on demonstrations, and run the program design workshop without rushing.

Can we book a private session for our team?

Yes. If you have a team of 8 or more, we can run a dedicated session tailored to your ground conditions, the fluids you're using, and the applications your crew works in. Get in touch to discuss.

Do I need any prior knowledge?

No. Sessions are designed for all experience levels. Experienced drillers and new operators both get value — the conversations between them are often the best part.

Is there a certificate or CPD credit?

We issue a completion record that can be used for your own training records. We're working towards formal CPD accreditation — register your interest and we'll keep you informed as that progresses.
